articles.title: ‘Pakistan don’t offer much competition’: BCCI takes swipe after Asian Games final
articles.summary: BCCI president Mithun Manhas praised India’s handling of pressure in the Asian Games 2026 men’s cricket final against Pakistan, while taking a dig at the
articles.body: BCCI president Mithun Manhas praised India’s handling of pressure in the Asian Games 2026 men’s cricket final against Pakistan, while taking a dig at the quality of competition offered by the arch-rivals in recent years.India secured one of their 21 gold medals at the Games after beating Pakistan by 19 runs in the final on Saturday, October 3, at the Korakuen Stadium in Nisshin, Japan. The closely fought contest saw Pakistan push India hard during the chase, but the defending champions held their nerve to retain the gold medal.Manhas, however, felt the result also highlighted what he believes is a decline in the competitiveness of India-Pakistan contests.“They defeated arch-rivals Pakistan, who I feel don't offer much competition anymore, and the way our team handled pressure situations... no other team in the world can do that," Manhas said after the final.The BCCI president also lauded India’s overall campaign, insisting that the team deserved its status as the tournament’s best side."By far the best team of the tournament. We are the defending champions, and the performance they have shown this time is commendable,” he added.Abhishek sets the tone, Tilak finishes stronglyAbhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma played key roles in India’s imposing total of 211, with both batters registering half-centuries.Manhas highlighted the contribution of the two batters and explained how India’s top and middle order combined to put Pakistan under pressure.“This is a team sport. Tilak Varma batted brilliantly, and Abhishek Sharma set the tone for the game. The job of openers is to build the innings, and the middle order finishes it. So, the openers basically set the tone," Manhas said.Abhishek gave India an explosive start, scoring 61 off 28 balls, while Tilak struck 51 off 22. India lost wickets during the middle overs but recovered through Tilak and Shivam Dube, who added 62 runs off 30 balls for the sixth wicket.“Team India's batting has been tremendous, and as for the bowling, I would say everyone contributed together to defend a good total,” the former Delhi batter added.Bowlers hold their nerveIndia’s 211 was the first total above 200 in the tournament. Pakistan, though, mounted a serious challenge in the chase, led by Hasan Nawaz, who smashed 96 off 51 deliveries.India’s bowlers eventually managed to keep Pakistan to 182/6 after 20 overs, securing a 19-run victory. Axar Patel and Washington Sundar claimed two wickets each, while Jasprit Bumrah went wicketless but played a crucial role by bowling effectively during tense phases of the chase.The victory gave India back-to-back Asian Games cricket gold medals after their triumph in the previous edition.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'India's Got Latent' Gambit? Behind Vantika Agrawal's double bronze at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad in Uzbekistan's Samarkand, like usual, had just one rest day, after Round 6.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad in Uzbekistan's Samarkand, like usual, had just one rest day, after Round 6. Consequently, India's Vantika Agrawal, who had beaten US chess legend Irina Krush in that sixth-round matchup on Board 3, ended up with three days away from the board anyway — the scheduled rest day, plus two more rounds where she was kept off the lineup by captain Swayams Mishra, against Germany and Kazakhstan.Too much chess prep over those first two days had left Vantika looking for an escape on the third. Samay Raina's popular show 'India's Got Latent' came to her rescue. She binge-watched the latest episodes on her third day off, then returned to the board the next day and clinched a win over Uzbekistan's Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva in her Round 9 matchup."Usually I don't watch that much, because you don't get the time. You prepare in the morning, then at night you're checking your opponent and discussing, then preparing again in the morning. By the afternoon you have a game, and you're tired. But this time, with the rest day plus two more days off, I had a lot of time, and I thought I'd practised so much chess already; let me relax a bit. So I watched some India's Got Latent episodes," she told TimesofIndia.com.Asked if she enjoyed it, there was no hesitation. "Yes, of course," she added. "I'd watched earlier episodes too, and then the new one there. It's nice. You just relax a bit."Vantika ended her campaign with a score of 6/8, five wins to her name, and an individual bronze medal in India women's bronze-clinching campaign. It's the quieter of India's two medal stories from this Olympiad, and arguably the more interesting one to hear told from the inside."I think it was good," she said of the experience overall. "I mean, of course, last time I won double gold. So this time also, we went for the gold, and it wasn't like we planned. We lost at the start to Poland. It wasn't as smooth as last year. But I'm glad that we won a lot of games and had a comeback, and managed to end on the podium; after a setback, we were able to come back and keep going. I think that was really important."The one that got awayIf there's a single result Vantika would look back with some disappointment, it's the Round 10 draw against China that effectively ended India's gold-medal hopes. The 24-year-old lost her game to Lu Miaoyi on Board 3, with the team setting for a 2-2 draw."I was especially very upset about my game against China," the International Master (IM) admitted. "I think I was playing quite well, and after 40 moves it was very drawish. There were a lot of ways to make a draw. But somehow I was playing for a win at that moment. I knew my position wasn't better, but I decided to play for a win. Because of that, I made some foolish decisions."Part of the problem, she explained, was not knowing the full picture elsewhere. "At that moment it wasn't clear that we were winning on the fourth board, or I would have just gone for a draw. I was not sure what was happening on that board, and I thought I would play for a win," she recalled."Except for my loss against China, I think it was pretty good. Before that, I was on 5.5 out of 6. I had almost won all my games. If not for that loss, I would have even got an individual gold on board."I won against Krush. Then, after three days of rest, I won against an Uzbek player, also quite strong. So I think it was good, except one game I wasn't happy about."Shaking off a bad result, she said, came down to a fairly simple discipline as she added, "I think it was just to focus on the next game, and not really think about what had already happened."A team built for the challengesVantika credited the dressing room, and Mishra specifically, for how the team absorbed the Poland loss and kept pushing."They all were very nice. Humpy (Koneru) was playing so well on board, Divya (Deshmukh), Savitha (Shri). Everyone was playing well. I think it can be seen that, in the end, we all won individual medals on our board," she remarked."We were kind of prepared for that, because last year also we lost to Poland and had that setback. So we were prepared that if something goes wrong, we will come together and fight as a team."That same candour extended to the one selection question hanging over the campaign, which was Vaishali Rameshbabu's dip in form, which saw her dropped for the final rounds."She is so strong she won the Candidates and is now the World Championship challenger. If she was in her full form, we would have easily crushed everyone. Those little chances that other teams got, like Poland, I don't think they would have got — we'd be winning on all boards," Vantika said.Asked whether the team dwells on these swings and misses while they're actually happening, Vantika was clear that they deliberately don't."I don't think we really think about that. Everyone tries to focus just on their own game, and our coach decides who plays, who doesn't, so that everything goes well. We don't think that much about these things," she added."Last time we had crushed everyone. We were 7 on 7, winning every game, not giving anyone a chance. This time it wasn't the same, even though we went with our best team. So the difficult part was accepting that every time you can't win gold, you can't crush everyone. It happens. That acceptance. That was difficult."The IM looking to make a mark in elite circuitWhen she was asked why she had been less visible on the elite circuit, Vantika Agrawal, already an Arjuna Awardee, was quick to push back on the perception that hers had been a quiet year outside the Olympiad bubble."I'm not invited to these top tournaments where the other girls, Humpy, Vaishali, Divya, are playing," she told this website. "But it's not that I'm not active. I'm playing a lot of open tournaments, and I'd say I'm more active than them. If you check my profile, I've played more games than any of them. It's just that I'm not playing in the tournaments everyone covers.""My rating is a bit low, and it's not easy to increase — even when I play very well, I gain maybe five or seven rating points. It's not easy to reach that level, and only once you reach it do you get invited to those tournaments," she further noted."This year I beat Song Yuxin; she played board two for China, in an open tournament. I beat Aditya Mittal too, who's over 2600 and hadn't lost a game all year before that — he just lost to me."There was a touch of frustration in how she recalled one particular near-miss for recognition."In the Tata Steel Rapid and Blitz in January, I tied for first place in Blitz, tied with Carissa Yip. But nobody covered that. It's just not being covered," she added with some disappointment.Whatever the coverage gap, Vantika insists it hasn't dented her own sense of where she stands and what she is aiming for — a Grandmaster (GM) title."I already feel confident, and I'm continuously working. It didn't change much after this Olympiad. I just want to focus on my goals and not think too much about all this," she added. "I'll continue playing more tournaments, trying to improve my skills and my level."Life after the board, and 2027Looking to 2027, her plan is a continuation rather than a reinvention. "I think I'll be doing the same thing, playing these open tournaments and trying to increase my rating, and see how it pans out," she admitted.ALSO READ: ‘Sometimes in chess, there are just these blind spots’: Nihal Sarin looks back at his Chess Olympiad loss to Uzbekistan | ExclusiveHer studies, meanwhile, are largely settled. "I've completed my B.Com Honours. I was at SRCC College, Delhi University. After that, I've been focusing more on chess, because I had exams in December that clashed with tournaments I really wanted to play. articles.title: The Super League Grand Final winner without a contract for 2027: Wakefield Trinity's Lachlan Walmsley lives out dream but uncertainty lies ahead
articles.summary: Lachlan Walmsley came up with an assist in the Super League Grand Final but is without a contract for 2027; he was part of the Wakefield side that made history and ended a 58-year top-flight trophy drought
articles.body:
Walmsley was part of the Wakefield side that made history with their 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Super League Grand Final to become only the sixth winners of the competition.

It ended a 58-year top-flight trophy drought for a side that have gone through everything Super League has had to offer. From at one point struggling to keep the lights on, they are now at the top of the sport.

During that game, winger Walmsley came up with an audacious no-look flick pass to set up Wakefield's opening try for Cam Scott. It was his farewell to a club that have given him so much.

Prior to living out his dream, Walmsley made a handful of appearances in the second division of Australian rugby before deciding to chase the dream on the other side of the world.

He gambled on a move to the UK with Championship side Whitehaven before joining Halifax Panthers were he scored 68 tries in 54 games and earned recognition.

That caught the eye of Wakefield as they entered the Championship following their relegation in 2023. It was Walmsley's first full-time contract.

Three seasons later, he is a Grand Final champion.

But now, once emotions subside his focus will have to turn to trying to get a contract for next season. Part of Walmsley's problem is he takes up a quota spot for clubs.

"Hopefully something will come through in the next couple of weeks," Walmsley said.

"I have already had a dig at both Matt [Ellis] and Powelly [Daryl Powell] and said surely one more year won't hurt.

"I don't know. I haven't really thought about it. I have kind of put it in the back of my mind because, obviously, the Grand Final's coming up.

"I will leave it to my agent and see what he can get. I have got a good mate in France who wants me to come play there. I might go play a bit, but we'll see what happens.

"If I wasn't on a quota spot, I'd probably get a few offers. It is just because I'm a quota. It just is what it is, isn't it?"

Despite the uncertainty around his future, Walmsley knows he is a perfect example of someone taking a leap, putting the work in, and it paying off.

"Obviously chase your dreams and anything can happen. A bit of luck involved, but you take what you get," Walmsley added.

"Coming from Whitehaven and then Halifax for a couple of years and just to be here now and have that ring on my finger.

Whatever happens, Walmsley will forever be one of Wakefield's immortals.

articles.title: Ibrahimovic celebra los 45 años a su manera: con un nuevo Ferrari que reinará en su garaje
articles.standfirst: Zlatan ha recibido un espectacular Ferrari F80 de cuatro millones de euros por su cumpleaños
articles.summary: Zlatan ha recibido un espectacular Ferrari F80 de cuatro millones de euros por su cumpleaños
articles.body: Cada vez que se lee en la cuenta de Instagram de Zlatan Ibrahimovic las palabras "Happy Birthday to Zlatan", Ferrari hace caja. Y este año 2026 no ha sido diferente porque el ex delantero de Barcelona, Milán y Juve (entre otros), se ha regalado el Ferrari más bestia que existe: el F80. El hecho de que el sueco sea embajador de Volvo no le ha impedido engordar su garaje, plagado de los Ferrari más caros y exclusivos, con la última joya de Maranello. Desde ayer. el día de su 45 cumpleaños, el genial delantero de Malmoe ya es uno de los 799 afortunados propietarios del último Special Series de Ferrari. Eso sí, ha tenido que esperar todo un año porque justamente el pasado octubre ya anunciaba a sus aficionados que su siguiente adquisición sería un F80. Ferrari se puso las pilas y, con buena vista, ha hecho coincidir su llegada con el aniversario del delantero. Ibrahimovic disfrutará de un biplaza híbrido enchufable de 1.200 caballos de potencia que, como es fácil deducir, le convierten en el Ferrari más rápido de la historia en la pista de Fiorano. Acelera de 0 a 100 en 2,75 segundos y su velocidad máxima es de 350 km/h... y porque está limitada. Todo esto quizá sea suficiente para compensar que su motor térmico sea sólo un V6, aunque está apoyado por otros tres eléctricos para llegar a esos 1.200 caballos. Como ya sucedía con el SF90 Stradale, el F80 es un Ferrari que también puede moverse en completo silencio, propulsado únicamente por electricidad. La colección de Ferrari del sueco ya acumula piezas tan impactantes como el Daytona SP3, el 812 Competizione, el SF90 XX y otro SF90 Spyder 'convencional', un Purosangue, o un Monza SP2. Eso sí, el F80 va a ocupar un lugar protagonista en ese museo automovilísitico del cavallino.

articles.title: Embarrassing scenes at Sepang as Hamilton and several drivers suddenly stop on track
articles.summary: The starting procedure has been suspended, with several cars, including Lewis Hamilton's, coming to a halt on track, resulting in a further delay to the star...
articles.body:
The starting procedure has been suspended, with several cars, including Lewis Hamilton's, coming to a halt on track, resulting in a further delay to the start of the Bahrain Grand Prix .

The seven-time world champion reported over the radio that he was unable to accelerate, forcing him to stop on track. Hamilton was eventually able to get going again after carrying out a software reset. Max Verstappen experienced a similar issue, although the Dutchman managed to continue without coming to a complete stop.

Esteban Ocon and Valtteri Bottas also encountered problems, bringing his car to a halt before eventually managing to resume. The cars have now returned to the pit lane before heading back onto the circuit for another attempt at beginning the race.

articles.title: Summer arrival could eventually open the door for major Real Madrid exit – report
articles.summary: One of the major talking points surrounding Real Madrid in the summer was the contractual situation involving Vinicius Junior.The Brazilian was entering the...
articles.body:
One of the major talking points surrounding Real Madrid in the summer was the contractual situation involving Vinicius Junior.

The Brazilian was entering the final year of his contract at the Santiago Bernabeu, and the negotiations did not prove to be straightforward.

Eventually, Los Blancos accepted more than they initially offered to get Vinicius to put pen to paper on a new contract with Madrid.

However, the club's decision to invest heavily in Yan Diomande could eventually have consequences for Vinicius Junior, particularly if the Brazilian continues to struggle to rediscover his best form.

According to Defensa Central , the arrival of Diomande has created a potential scenario in which Madrid could become more receptive to a future Vinicius departure.

The club are not actively looking to sell him at the moment, but Madrid's attacking riches mean no player is untouchable.

Vinicius Jr. is having a difficult time at Real Madrid. (Photo by Albert Perez/Getty Images)

Diomande's emergence matters because he can operate from the left, the area Vinicius has made his own at the Bernabeu.

The 19-year-old has already shown enough to demand more opportunities , while Arda Guler has also strengthened his claim for a significant attacking role.

Vinicius, meanwhile, has endured a difficult start to the season. Mourinho has publicly supported him and maintained that rediscovering his best football is a matter of time.

However, there is only so long that Mourinho can keep faith in the Brazilian if the performances do not back it up.

A major offer could change Madrid's position

Vinicius' recent renewal makes an immediate departure unlikely. A sufficiently large offer, however, could potentially force Madrid to consider their options.

Much would depend on the Brazilian himself. If Vinicius rediscovers the intensity and decisive quality that helped Madrid win major trophies, there is little reason to push him out.

Diomande is emerging as a real option for Real Madrid. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

However, if his difficulties continue while Diomande develops rapidly, the conversation inevitably becomes different.

For years, Vinicius' importance to Madrid made his position virtually unquestionable. The squad Mourinho now possesses means that status can no longer be taken entirely for granted.

Diomande is young, explosive and already pushing for minutes. Madrid also have other attacking pieces capable of assuming greater responsibility.

An exit for Vinicius would not come as a total surprise if things do not improve, and it remains to be seen how things pan out.

articles.title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia descends into chaos as car trouble prompts red flag
articles.summary: Suspected power unit gremlins for a number of cars, including Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, forced Formula 1 race control to suspend the start of a wet Bahrain G...
articles.body:
The Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia has been red-flagged after several cars suffered power unit gremlins during a wet set of formation laps.

After a heavy tropical thunderstorm, the action at Malaysian Sepang was set to get underway with a number of laps behind the safety car followed by a standing start.

But ahead of F1's first-ever wet event under the 2026 regulations, a number of cars suffered power unit gremlins in the rain, suspected to be software-related.

Initially, polesitter Max Verstappen reported a lack of acceleration from his Red Bull before the Dutchman got going again. Soon after, second-placed Lewis Hamilton reported a similar issue on his Ferrari, with the Briton crawling around the first formation lap as the rest of the field passed him. One lap later, Hamilton too managed to get going again.

More cars, including Racing Bulls man Liam Lawson, Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, also appeared to struggle with similar problems, with race control suspending the start procedure and throwing a red flag.

With the grid mixed up as cars streamed into pitlane, race control will revert to the original grid positions when the running is resumed.

articles.title: “Unbearable To Listen To”: Fans Push Back Against Gus Johnson After Wrong Call During Michigan vs Minnesota Matchup
articles.summary: Gus Johnson miscalled a play during Michigan’s game against Minnesota on Saturday. The veteran announcer thought Michigan freshman running back Savion Hiter...
articles.body:
Gus Johnson miscalled a play during Michigan's game against Minnesota on Saturday. The veteran announcer thought Michigan freshman running back Savion Hiter had the ball on what was actually a keeper by sophomore quarterback Bryce Underwood.

The option-style play occurred near midfield with Michigan trailing 7-0. Johnson failed to track the ball and thought Underwood had handed it off.

Fans quickly reacted to the moment, calling for Johnson to be taken off air.

"I'm not sure this is even a hot take these days, but Gus Johnson is unbearable to listen to on football broadcasts," one fan added.

The above game at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis was broadcast nationally by FOX, with Johnson on play-by-play, Joel Klatt as the analyst and Jenny Taft reporting from the sideline.

Johnson is best known for his dramatic play-by-play commentary on college football and basketball for FOX Sports. Before joining FOX Sports, he called NCAA Tournament games, NFL games and college football for CBS Sports.

In the 100th Little Brown Jug rivalry game on Saturday, Michigan led Minnesota 14-7 at halftime at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis.

The Golden Gophers opened the scoreboard with a rushing touchdown by Darius Taylor in the first quarter. Michigan rebounded strongly with two touchdowns in the second quarter. At 13:46, Jordan Marshall rushed for a 5-yard touchdown.

With over two minutes to play in the first half, Michigan intercepted Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey's pass and returned it for a touchdown to end the half 14-7.

The Wolverines entered the game 3-1 after their dramatic 20-19 loss to Iowa. Minnesota is also 3-1 after beating Washington 27-24 on the road.

articles.title: Marquez wins in Japan to cut Martin's MotoGP lead
articles.summary: Defending MotoGP champion Marc Marquez wins a sprint-race double at the Japanese Grand Prix to cut Jorge Martin's championship lead to two points.
articles.body:
Reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez took maximum points at the Japanese Grand Prix, winning Saturday's sprint and Sunday's race, to cut fellow Spaniard Jorge Martin's championship lead to just two points.

Martin, 28, who won the title in 2024, finished second after starting Sunday's race at Motegi Circuit in pole position, while his Aprilla team-mate Marco Bezzecchi was third.

Ducati rider Marquez, 33, had to bide his time after Martin held his advantage off the line, but the seven-time champion took his chance on the 11th lap to edge past his rival on the inside.

"The race was tough, especially when I was behind Jorge, but I knew that if I was able to lead the race, my pace was good," said Marquez, who moved to 331 points with six rounds remaining.

"Jorge tried to attack, but then I just increased a bit more the pace and it was enough to do the last two laps more relaxed."

Italian Bezzecchi, 27, moved to 284 points to keep his slim title hopes alive after fending off a late charge by Tech3's Enea Bastianini to claim his place on the podium.

Gresini's Alex Marquez had a race to forget, crashing out after serving a double long lap penalty for his role in a three-rider collision during Saturday's sprint.

articles.title: Rafael Nadal shares whether his plans to become a coach in the future have changed, ‘never say never’
articles.summary: Rafael Nadal remains a hugely relevant figure in the tennis world, even now, nearly two years on from his retirement. That is likely why his...
articles.body:
Rafael Nadal remains a hugely relevant figure in the tennis world, even now, nearly two years on from his retirement.

That is likely why his recent exhibition match, his first since calling time on his career, was so sought after, as he played alongside Andy Murray among other legends of their generation and beyond in honour of the ten-year anniversary of his academy.

He clearly boasts a great friendship with the Scotsman, who seemingly rushed back into coaching not long after his retirement.

And now, speaking to the media, Rafael Nadal has discussed whether he has any interest in following in these footsteps.

Rafael Nadal refuses to rule out coaching in the future

Discussing this topic back in July, Nadal insisted he had no time for coaching , but was happy to help any player who needed it.

This open invitation has been taken up by some big-name stars, most notably Alexander Zverev. Iga Swiatek did also train with Nadal earlier this year, likely aided by his relationship with Francisco Roig, her coach.

However, when asked again this weekend about whether his opinion on the matter had changed, he reiterated: "To be a coach? Never say never. But, I have two young children.

"I have many other things in my life today that occupy me on a daily basis, so I don't think that my current life allows me to be or imagine being a coach in the way that it requires to be a good coach and dedicate yourself professionally to serving a professional player as they deserve.

"So it's not in my head at all right now. I don't know in five years from now what might happen."

Then, speaking about how it felt to be back on court again, the Spaniard admitted that whilst it was fun, it did bring back some painful memories.

Nadal added: "Grabbing the racquet will always be fun for me, but that's another matter from closing the door on exhibitions – I'll play them, but it's a slow process."

"In the end, I finished my career with a lot of physical problems; the racquet reminds me of many of the pains I went through. I can live better than I expected, and for me, that's very important after spending so many years living something else."

Nadal won his own Rafa Nadal Academy Slam over Murray, which was formatted over seven first-to-ten-point doubles matches, each with different partners.

The 22-time Grand Slam champion had a team boasting Carlos Moyà, David Ferrer and Richard Gasquet, whilst Murray had Marat Safin, Fabio Fognini and Dominic Thiem on his side.

articles.title: Leeds United’s Jean-Mattéo Bahoya sustains injury with France’s U21s
articles.summary: Jean-Mattéo Bahoya (21) is the latest victim of what has been a costly international window for France’s U21s. The Leeds United attacking midfielder joins th...
articles.body:
Jean-Mattéo Bahoya (21) is the latest victim of what has been a costly international window for France's U21s. The Leeds United attacking midfielder joins the likes of Ethan Mbappé, Senny Mayulu, and Ewen Jaouen in sustaining an injury while away with Les Bleuets.

Mbappé and Mayulu sustained injuries during the game against Estonia at the end of last month. Both are out for several weeks, whilst Jaouen suffered a hamstring injury during Thursday's training session.

Bahoya's injury came from an impact in the game against Luxembourg (3-2) on Saturday night. The attacking midfielder did recover before being forced to withdraw in the 37th minute. He was replaced by Tottenham Hotspur's Mathys Tel. Speaking post-match, France U21 manager Gérald Baticle said that he was not in a position to diagnose the injury, beyond stating that it was the ankle that was affected and that there would be further tests on the injury.

articles.title: 5 standout performers from Week 6 of Wichita Falls high school football
articles.summary: Check out five Wichita Falls-area football players who stood out in Week 6, including Memorial's Cole Birkhead and Legacy's Knox Hodges.
articles.body:
Week 6 turned another round of big individual performances across the Wichita Falls-area high school football landscape.

Cole Birkhead and Knox Hodges helped their respective Wichita Falls Class 5A programs earn district wins, while Jaxon Carrington rushed for three touchdowns in a statement victory for Seymour.

Isaac Ybarra powered Early to another victory on the ground, and Keegen Voyles delivered one of the most dramatic plays of the season for Newcastle.

Here are five standout performers from Week 6.

Petrolia vs Archer City high school football

Birkhead helped Memorial get back on track with a 59-7 victory against Lubbock Coronado, giving the Mavericks their first District 2-5A Division II win of the season.

The senior quarterback threw four touchdown passes, connecting twice with Clayton Brumley and twice with Krew Bailey. His scoring throws went for 7, 8, 14 and 74 yards.

Birkhead helped Memorial build a 36-0 halftime lead and improve to 3-3 overall after opening district play with a tough loss to Abilene Cooper.

Hodges facilitated Legacy's offense Friday night, helping the Leopards snap a two-game losing streak with a 37-14 road victory against Lubbock-Cooper.

The junior quarterback threw two touchdown passes, connecting with Ben Barnard for a 3-yard score in the first quarter before finding Jourian Wiggins for another touchdown early in the second.

The Leopards built a 23-7 halftime lead behind Hodges and got their offense back on track after consecutive losses to Greenwood and Amarillo Palo Duro. Legacy improved to 4-2 heading into its Week 7 bye.

Carrington rushed for 95 yards and three touchdowns on 13 carries in Seymour's 49-26 victory over previously unbeaten Munday.

His 11-yard touchdown run gave Seymour a 13-8 lead in the first quarter, and he later broke free for a 29-yard score before capping the Panthers' scoring with a 9-yard touchdown run.

Carrington's three-touchdown performance helped Seymour hand Munday its first loss of the season and improve to 4-2 overall and 2-0 in District 6-2A Division II play.

Ybarra powered Early's offense in a 45-20 victory over Bowie, helping the Longhorns bounce back from their first loss of the season.

The senior running back carried 25 times for 231 yards and three touchdowns, scoring on runs of 32, 44 and 50 yards.

Ybarra's production helped Early erase an early deficit and improve to 5-1 heading into district play.

Voyles delivered the biggest play of Week 6 in Newcastle's 58-52 win over Jayton.

With the game tied 52-52 and Jayton threatening to score in the final seconds, Voyles intercepted a pass near the goal line and returned it 79 yards for the game-winning touchdown.

The play ended Jayton's 34-game winning streak and handed the Jaybirds their first loss since 2023, while Newcastle improved to 4-1.

articles.summary: Week 6 of Texoma high school football brought bounce-back wins, an upset of unbeaten Munday and a wild Newcastle finish. Here are five key takeaways.
articles.body:
Week 6 of the 2026 high school football season offered more clarity as district races began taking shape across the Texoma region.

Memorial and Legacy responded to losses with convincing victories; Seymour knocked off an unbeaten opponent, and a pair of area teams continued impressive starts to the season.

Here are five things we learned from Week 6 of Wichita Falls-area high school football.

Petrolia vs Archer City high school football

Newcastle entered Friday facing a Jayton program that hadn't lost a football game since 2023.

That streak ended in about as dramatic a fashion as possible.

With the score tied at 52 and Jayton threatening in the final seconds, Newcastle's Keegen Voyles intercepted a pass near the goal line and returned it 79 yards for the game-winning touchdown. The 58-52 victory snapped Jayton's 34-game winning streak, which included two state championships.

The significance goes beyond Newcastle just moving to 4-1. The Bobcats showed they can execute in high-pressure situations against Texas' best, giving them a victory that carries massive weight as the season presses on.

Memorial entered Friday looking for a response after opening District 2-5A Division II play with a 49-28 loss to Abilene Cooper. The Mavericks got one in emphatic fashion.

Memorial (3-3) rolled past Lubbock Coronado 59-7 en route to its first District 2-5A Division II victory of the year. Coronado entered the matchup at 1-4, but that certainly doesn't diminish the significance of the win.

The decisive victory pushed the Mavericks back to .500 and showed they still have plenty to play for as district action ramps up.

Legacy came into Friday's matchup on a two-game losing streak after falling 43-42 to Greenwood and 50-9 to Amarillo Palo Duro.

The Leopards (4-2) responded with a 37-14 road victory over Lubbock-Cooper to earn their first District 2-5A Division II win of the season — and just their second in the young program's history. Knox Hodges threw two touchdown passes as Legacy built a 23-7 halftime advantage.

After managing only nine points against Palo Duro, Legacy's offense looked much more like itself on Friday. The Leopards now head into their Week 7 bye with a chance to build on that performance before returning to district play.

Seymour belongs in the district conversation

Seymour entered Friday with an opportunity to make a real move in District 6-2A Division II, and an unbeaten Munday team gave it the perfect test.

The Panthers pulled away for a 49-26 victory, handing the Moguls their first loss of the season and improving to 4-2 overall and 2-0 in district play. Jaxon Carrington led the way with 95 yards and three touchdowns on 13 carries, scoring on runs of 9, 11 and 29 yards — his longest run of the night.

The win knocked off a 5-0 opponent, kept the Panthers perfect in league play and added real weight to the rest of their district schedule.

Isaac Ybarra gave Early exactly what it needed after the Longhorns fell behind early against a 4-1 Bowie team.

The senior running back carried 25 times for 231 yards and three touchdowns, scoring on runs of 32, 44 and 50 yards as Early (5-1) scored 31 unanswered points to turn a 14-7 deficit into a 45-20 victory.

The Longhorns also forced four second-half turnovers, giving the offense short-field advantages and helping turn a competitive game into a comfortable win.

More importantly, Early showed it can win with a clear formula: lean on Ybarra, create takeaways and wear teams down as the game goes on.
authors: Andy Mathis, Wichita Falls Times Record News

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc arrive at Sepang in matching sports saloons
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have arrived at Sepang in matching Alfa Romeo Giulia Veloces
articles.body:
Your Ferrari drivers don't usually disappoint us with what they drive to race weekends. Whether it be a classic Ferrari supercar or a Ducati superbike, it usually leaves us fans drooling with jealousy. This weekend in Malaysia was no different as Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc arrived in matching sports saloons from Alfa Romeo.

The Scuderia pair was spotted driving Alfa Romeo Giulia Veloces, Hamilton finished in Misano Blue and his team-mate's in the brand's signature Alfa Rosso red.

The Veloce is the only trim level that Malaysia sells of this model, but that doesn't mean it's limited in other ways. It featured a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder producing 276 horsepower and 400 Nm of torque. That power is transmitted to the rear wheels through an 8-speed automatic gearbox and a limited-slip differential. It's not quick by modern standards, with 0 to 100 km/h taking 5.7 seconds and top speed sat at 240 km/h.

Inside you get beautiful aluminium paddle shifters behind the steering wheel and a 14-speaker Harman Kardon sound system - we know both the Ferrari drivers love their music.

Ferrari and Alfa Romeo aren't just neighbouring Italian brands. The two have been intertwined throughout their Italian automotive and motorsport history. Enzo Ferrari himself raced an Alfa Romeo in the 1920s before founding Scuderia Ferrari in 1929, and even then, Ferrari was racing Alfa Romeo machinery. The Scuderia supplied the drivers and the racing operation while Alfa Romeo supplied the cars.

By 1947, the Prancing Horse brand had started building its own racing cars and had moved away from Alfa Romeo chassis, and by the start of the Formula 1 world championship in 1950, it was its own racing entity. Now, it's the oldest surviving team in F1. In that first year of the championship, though, Alfa Romeo was incredibly dominant with its drivers Juan Manuel Fangio and Giuseppe Farina, with the latter winning the title.

articles.title: ‘Not a backup’- Jameis Winston sends message as J.J. McCarthy arrival increases QB pressure
articles.summary: Jameis Winston has made it clear he no longer sees himself as a backup after taking over as the New York Giants’ starting quarterback, despite the recent arr...
articles.body:
Jameis Winston has made it clear he no longer sees himself as a backup after taking over as the New York Giants' starting quarterback, despite the recent arrival of J.J. McCarthy.

Winston stepped into the starting role after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury, leading the Giants to a 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans. However, his position now comes with added pressure following New York's trade for McCarthy.

The Giants acquired the former Minnesota Vikings quarterback for a 2027 fifth-round pick on September 28. McCarthy has initially landed behind Winston and Jake Haener, but his arrival has naturally raised questions about the future of the position.

Jameis Winston refuses to accept backup label

During post-practice media availability ahead of their Week 4 clash, Winston was quick to correct a reporter who referred to him in the context of developing backup quarterbacks.

"I've never said something to that manner… Like, I don't have any place for excuses. It's our job, right?" Winston said. "It's a privilege, whatever role that you get. And you keep saying backup—I'm not a backup no more. I'm a starter, so I'm getting the first team reps like the majority of them now."

Winston also insisted that McCarthy's arrival has not made him feel disrespected. Instead, he described the competition as a challenge to improve.

"I feel challenged to get better every single day. So, I just think that's the makeup of who I am as a person. Always looking for ways to build on the positives and eliminate the negatives," he said.

Winston has completed just 51.1% of his passes this season and has a 22.9 QBR, while the Giants have scored only 18 points across their last two games, all through field goals. He also recorded just 118 passing yards against Tennessee, although the Giants secured the win.

Coach John Harbaugh has backed the veteran, while offensive coordinator Matt Nagy also expressed confidence in him.

For now, McCarthy is learning the offence as the third-string quarterback. But Winston knows the equation is simple: he has to play well enough to keep the Giants from considering a change.

"I have to play well regardless. That's it," Winston said. "It doesn't matter who's in the building. When you're the quarterback for the New York Football Giants, you have to give your team a chance to win."

The Giants take on Cardinals in their Week 4 clash at MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford.

articles.title: Man City signing Sullivan becomes youngest US goalscorer
articles.summary: Cavan Sullivan becomes the youngest US international goalscorer in history with a stunning lob in a 3-0 friendly win over rivals Mexico.
articles.body:
Cavan Sullivan became the youngest US international goalscorer in history with a stunning lob in a 3-0 friendly win over rivals Mexico.

Mathis Albert, at 17 years and 131 days, had set the mark with his goal against Chile on Wednesday, but his record lasted for just five days as Sullivan struck gold.

At 17 years and five days old, Sullivan - who is set to join Manchester City next season - intercepted a pass from Raul Rangel and perfectly lobbed the Mexico goalkeeper in the 62nd minute to double the USA's lead.

"These are the moments you dream of when you're a three, four, five or six-year-old," Sullivan said.

"I manifested this moment, not just these past couple of hours when I found out I was starting, but my whole life."

Sullivan, who currently plays for MLS club Philadelphia Union, is poised to join Manchester City next season after the English club secured his signature as a 14-year-old back in 2024.

However, there is uncertainty over the move after City were found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching. The club are expected to appeal.

Sullivan's chipped goal against Mexico came after another teenager - 18-year-old Julian Hall - had given Mauricio Pochettino's side the lead in the 28th minute.

"I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn't hit the crossbar or go over," Sullivan said.

"I was getting nervous when it was in the air and then everything was a blur."

Mexico's evening in Arizona went from bad to worse when substitute Luis Chavez was shown a red card for shoving his hand into the face of Sebastian Berhalter in the 68th minute, while Malik Tillman completed the scoring 16 minutes later.

articles.title: ‘It’s a big test’ – Spurs facing another tough test against London City Lionesses says Ho
articles.summary: Tottenham Hotspur head coach Martin Ho says that his side will face another big test when they play host to London City Lionesses afternoon.The Lilywhites we...
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur head coach Martin Ho says that his side will face another big test when they play host to London City Lionesses afternoon.

The Lilywhites welcome The Pride to the BetWright Stadium for their latest Barclays Women's Super League match.

Both sides have started the season well and could challenge at the top end of the Barclays Women's Super League table. When speaking in the pre-match press conference, Spurs boss Ho said that London City Lionesses will provide his side with another stern challenge.

"It's a big test, but every game now is tough," Ho said. "We've seen that in midweek against Brighton with a new manager and a new look and we faced it against Aston Villa, Crystal Palace and so on.

"We've faced tough games. You'll have to be at your best in every game or you're going to come up short. We saw that against West Ham in the cup.

"It's going to be a tough test, but one that we are relishing."

Going on to discuss London City Lionesses, Ho acknowledged The Pride's world-class talent, but said that Spurs will be focusing on themselves.

He said "They've got individual qualities, you've seen that throughout the years they've been going. They definitely have more of a balance of youth and older international experience now with the players that they've brought in.

"What they have is a breadth of world-class talent in their team, but what we will do is focus on ourselves and what we need to do to apply ourselves to put our imprint on the game. They will need to think about what we are doing as well as what they're going to do."

Spurs face London City Lionesses, Chelsea and Arsenal in consecutive games and Ho is confident that his side will keep pushing hard for success.

He said "We can compete against anyone in this league. We have this stigma in this league that only the 'top three' are unbeatable, but it's not what it is and we need to look at it slightly different.

"There's a difference between ambition and expectation. Our ambitions are always high and will be high to make sure we can achieve what we want to achieve and compete at the top of the table, but the expectation has got to be clear; success isn't linear all of the time and sustaining long-term success isn't linear.

"We have to make sure that we keep pushing and evolving as we are and I have no doubt that we will achieve what we want to achieve."

Tottenham Hotspur's Barclays Women's Super League fixture against London City Lionesses kicks-off at 2pm this afternoon.
